_meta.companion: data/telescopes/lbt.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows elt.json and vista.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; lbt: title, telescope (machine-readable mirrors, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as 'lbt.<param>'), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/lbt/ (files reused from data/imaging/vst_lbc.md are byte-identical copies, marked in the cite). derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure (the caption is checked). INFERRED = a choice no source states. NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, approximately-equal sign, middle dot, plus-minus (to +/-), the degree sign, the ordinal sign and the ring operator used as a degree normalized; soft hyphens removed; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page and across consecutive page pairs (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF); HTML as tag-stripped text (tags to a space, tags removed) and raw source (UTF-8); .py as is.

lbt.title: Large Binocular Telescope (LBTO, Mt. Graham): two 8.4 m f/1.14 primaries on one mount; prime focus (LBC), direct Gregorian (MODS) and bent Gregorian (LUCI, LBTI, LINC-NIRVANA, PEPSI) foci; the single-side pupil and the two-mirror pupil of the combined-beam focus

telescope.name: Large Binocular Telescope (LBT): two 8.4 m telescopes on one mount (SX left, DX right)
telescope.site: Emerald Peak, Mt. Graham, Arizona (Mount Graham International Observatory), 3192 m (R16, GH09)
telescope.mount: alt-azimuth; both primaries on one mount, centers 14.417 m apart; swing arms carry the prime-focus cameras, the adaptive secondaries and the tertiaries (LQF, R16)
telescope.optical_design: for each side: an f/1.142 paraboloid; prime focus with a refractive corrector (LBC), or an f/15 Gregorian with an undersized adaptive concave secondary, straight through or folded by a flat tertiary to four bent Gregorian stations (LQF, R16)

tertiary.kind: flat ellipse on a swing arm

pupil.frame: x along the baseline toward DX (SX at -x); sky or focus view NOT FOUND

struts.basis: width and wedge B20; direction INFERRED (S18 Fig. 2)

prime.obstruction: NOT FOUND (the LBC body); eps >= 0.1058 (the 0.889 m hole)

foci.name: prime focus, LBC-Blue (SX)
foci.corrector: Wynne type: five fused-silica lenses + cryostat window (L1 810 mm)

foci.name: center bent Gregorian (LBTI, both mirrors)
foci.combined_focus: f/15 envelope (LTP, H16): f/15 on 22.65 m = 339.75 m, 0.6071"/mm, f/41.3 per mirror (DERIVED); NOMIC 0.600"/mm (DERIVED)
foci.cameras: LMIRCam 10.7 mas/px, ~22 arcsec; NOMIC 0.018 arcsec/px (17.9 mas), ~9 arcsec tall

foci.name: rear bent Gregorian (LINC-NIRVANA, both mirrors; optional)
fourth bent Gregorian (PEPSI fiber units; optional)

explorer_preset.name: LBT 2 × 8.4 m
explorer_preset.primaryNote: Two spin-cast borosilicate honeycomb paraboloids, 8.417 m across with 0.889 m central holes, f/1.142 (f = 9.6 m), on one alt-azimuth mount with their centers 14.4 m apart. Each side is a separate telescope; the left one (SX) is drawn. The adaptive secondary, a 0.911 m concave shell, is undersized: at the Gregorian foci the secondary is the stop and the pupil is 8.22 m.
explorer_preset.pupilNote: One side (SX) at the Gregorian foci: the 8.22 m pupil set by the undersized secondary, the secondary's 0.91 m shadow, and two 73 mm struts of the swing arms that meet at the center 18° apart (their direction, toward the outer edge of the mirror, is a reading of a photograph).

area.src: half of the 110 m² of the two mirrors (Green & Hill 2009; the 8.417 m mirror less the 0.889 m hole: 55.02 m², DERIVED); the 8.22 m Gregorian pupil drawn here: 51.9 m² (data/telescopes/lbt.md)

foci.name: Prime focus f/1.45 (LBC-Blue, SX)

corrector.label: LBC-Blue corrector
corrector.sub: five fused-silica lenses and the cryostat window, drawn as one lens

foci.secondary: none: the camera and its corrector ride on the prime-focus swing arm
foci.fieldNote: 27′ unvignetted (the corrected field is 110 mm across). F and the plate scale come from the corrector's 12.18 m focal length on 8.4 m. The LBC body's shadow is not published: ε is the primary's 0.889 m hole, a lower bound.

foci.name: Prime focus f/1.45 (LBC-Red, DX)

corrector.label: LBC-Red corrector
corrector.sub: five BK7 lenses and the cryostat window, drawn as one lens

foci.secondary: none: the camera and its corrector ride on the prime-focus swing arm
foci.fieldNote: 27′ (the corrected field is 108.2 mm across). F comes from the published 16.9″ per mm (12.2 m on 8.4 m). The right side (DX): the struts lie toward +x. The LBC body's shadow is not published: ε is the primary's hole.

foci.name: Direct Gregorian f/15 (MODS)
foci.secondary: the adaptive secondary: a concave 0.911 m shell with 672 actuators, undersized (the stop)
foci.where: 3.05 m behind the primary's vertex, straight through the primary's hole (MODS1 on SX, MODS2 on DX)
foci.fieldNote: 6′ × 6′ (MODS); the infrared field is unvignetted to 4′. f/15 is nominal: 123.9 m (f/14.72 on the 8.417 m parent) is f/15.07 on the 8.22 m pupil.

foci.name: Front bent Gregorian f/15 (LUCI)
foci.secondary: the adaptive secondary (0.911 m, the stop); a flat tertiary, 64 × 50 cm, 2.25 m above the primary
foci.where: the front bent Gregorian station (LUCI1 on SX, LUCI2 on DX); drawn in the plane of the baseline
foci.fieldNote: 4′ × 4′ (LUCI); the tertiary vignettes beyond 4.5′ from the axis. The focus 5.30 m from the axis is DERIVED (the tertiary's 2.25 m plus the 3.05 m back focal distance).

foci.name: Center bent Gregorian f/15 (LBTI, both mirrors)
foci.pupilNote: Both mirrors, centers 14.42 m apart and 22.64 m from edge to edge: the image of a star is the single-mirror pattern crossed by fringes along the baseline, three bright fringes within the core.
foci.secondary: the adaptive secondaries of both sides (0.911 m, the stops); flat tertiaries 2.25 m above the primaries
foci.where: between the two primaries: the LBTI beam combiner, with entrance windows at the two f/15 foci
foci.fieldNote: The beam combiner reimages the two f/15 foci onto one focal plane with an f/15 envelope: f/15 on the 22.65 m baseline (≈340 m, 0.61″ per mm), f/41 for each mirror. NOMIC: 0.018″ per 30 µm pixel; LMIRCam images the combined focus at 1:1, 10.7 mas per pixel over ≈22″. The phased field is of order 1′. Drawn: one side's f/15 focus at the entrance window.

The two 8.4 meter (331 inch) diameter primary mirrors are mounted with a 14.4 meter center-center separation.

primary_focal_ratio.derived: f1 = 1.142 x 8.417 m = 9.612 m if the ratio refers to the physical diameter (9.593 m on 8.4 m); no source gives the focal length or the radius of curvature. The explorer uses f1 = 9.612 m: F1 = 9.612/8.22 = 1.1693 on the Gregorian pupil, 9.612/8.4 = 1.1443 at prime focus. The real-ray pupil check (aperture_stop) favors 9.612 m.

swing_arms.value: three swing arms per side above each primary: (top to bottom) the adaptive secondary, the LBC prime-focus camera, the tertiary flat; swinging the arms changes the focus
swing_arms.quote: The swing arms are the three black structures hanging on each side of the mount above the primary mirrors. From top to bottom – The adaptive secondaries (in the beam on both sides) – The Large Binocular Cameras (out of the beam on both sides) – The tertiary flats (out of the beam on the left, in the beam on the right)

By using swing arms to rotate the secondary mirrors and their supports, it is possible to switch the telescope from one mode of observation to another very quickly.

alternatives.value: LBC on a spider swing arm
alternatives.quote: They are each mounted on a spider swing-arm that can be deployed above their respective primary mirror and moved into and out of the telescope beam as required.

secondary.value: adaptive Gregorian secondary: a concave Zerodur shell 0.911 m across and 1.6 mm thick, 672 actuators, conic -0.7328; undersized; on a swing arm
secondary.quote: Two Adaptive Secondary Mirrors Infrared Gregorian, F/15 Interchange: swing arm Mirror diameter: 0.911 m (undersized secondary) Mirror thickness: 1.6 mm

The wavefront corrector takes the form of a 672-actuator adaptive secondary mirror (ASM), also known as a deformable secondary mirror (DSM), mounted on each side of the LBT.

secondary.derived: Paraxial Gregorian (explorer model, imager.js greg): m = F/F1 = 15.073/1.1693 = 12.890; with the 3.050 m back focal distance, s = (m f1 + b)/(m - 1) = 10.677 m from the M1 vertex (1.065 m beyond the prime focus) and f2 = +0.988 m (R2 = 1.977 m, a concave prolate ellipsoid, consistent with conic -0.7328). The M1-M2 spacing and R2 are NOT FOUND in a source.

aperture_stop.derived: Real-ray trace (scratch script; M1 an exact paraboloid, M2 an ellipsoid of conic -0.7328 placed and curved by the paraxial Gregorian above, back focal distance 3.050 m): the axial ray that meets the edge of the 0.911 m secondary leaves M1 at 4.112 m from the axis for f1 = 9.612 m and fG = 123.51 m (MODS 1.67"/mm), so the pupil is 8.224 m; 8.252 m with fG = 123.90 m (f/14.72 on 8.417 m); 8.238-8.266 m with f1 = 9.593 m. The sag of M2 matters here: without the sag the same ray gives ~7.9 m.

Center spacing: 14.417 m (LQF optics list) vs 14.4 m (LQF text, R16, S18, G14).
Edge-to-edge baseline: 22.65 m (R16, GH09) vs 22.7 m (LTH Fizeau mode, H16) vs 22.8 m (LTH, LTM, B18, G14); DERIVED 22.637 m (Gregorian pupils) and 22.834 m (mirror rims).
Gregorian focal length: f/14.72 on the parent (LQF) = 123.90 m if on 8.417 m vs MODS FOCSCALE 1.67"/mm = 123.51 m; nominal f/15 (LQF, LUC, MOC, LTH).
Gregorian pupil: 8.22 m (A09, B19) vs 8.2 m (P17) vs DERIVED 8.22-8.27 m (real-ray trace).
LBC-Red: 16.9"/mm and f/1.47 in one sentence (LFP; 16.9"/mm is f/1.453 on 8.4 m, f/1.47 would be 12.35 m); LBC-Blue F/1.45 (G08) vs F/1.46 (G08, the detector paragraph of Sec. 2.1).
LBC corrected field: 110 mm and 108.2 mm, 'equivalent to 27 arcmin' (R16) vs 110 mm x 16.935"/mm = 31.0 arcmin (DERIVED) vs ~30 arcmin corrected and 27 arcmin unvignetted (G08).
LBTI combined focus: f/15 envelope = 339.75 m on 22.65 m (DERIVED) vs 2.75 x 123.90 m = 340.7 m (DERIVED from the ellipsoids) vs NOMIC 0.600"/mm = 343.8 m and 17.9 mas = 345.7 m (DERIVED).
Swing-arm diffraction: MM attributes the 'bunny ears' in saturated stars to the secondary swing arm (Sec. 2.6.4) and, later, to the rigid secondary (Sec. 2.12.3).
notes: Each side of the LBT is a separate telescope with an 8.417 m f/1.142 primary; the two share one mount, 14.4 m apart. The explorer draws one side (SX) at the chosen focus. The pupil at a single-side focus is one circle; at the LBTI focus a per-focus pupil override holds both mirrors (kind "circles", two 8.22 m circles centered at x = +/-7.2085 m, each with a 0.911 m central hole), so the diffraction-limited image shows the single-mirror envelope crossed by fringes along the baseline.

At the Gregorian foci the undersized 0.911 m adaptive secondary is the stop, so the pupil (8.22 m) is smaller than the mirror; at prime focus the primary is the stop (8.4 m nominal, as G08 uses for F/1.45).

The LBTI focus is entered at F 15.073 (the bent Gregorian focus of each side, at the LBTI entrance windows), so the drawing shows the real Gregorian geometry. The combined focus (f/15 on the 22.65 m envelope, f/41 on each mirror, 0.60"/mm) is in the fieldNote; an alternative entry with F 41.33 and plate 0.6071 draws a schematic Gregorian whose secondary sits 9.98 m from the primary (the real one: 10.68 m).
The single-side pupil is SX's (the struts toward -x); the DX prime focus (LBC-Red) overrides the vanes to +x. LUCI, MODS and LBC differ only slightly between the sides.
Optional further variants (same optics as the bent Gregorian front focus): the rear bent Gregorian (LINC-NIRVANA, both mirrors) and the fourth bent Gregorian (PEPSI fiber units, one pupil per side).
